meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Marshall Islands (Non-Resident Business Corporation regime, Majuro)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law foundation adopted from the United States corporate law model, with customary law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States of America (Amended 2003) - trade, investment and economic assistance provisions
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) framework and related Forum Economic Ministers Meeting commitments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of the Marshall Islands Financial Integrity Law 2020, as amended, and its implementing AML/CFT Regulations; Business Corporations Act 1990 (Title 39 of the RMI Revised Code), including share register and record-keeping duties; Banking Act 1991; directives and guidance issued by the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU); standards applicable through the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) membership

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Government-Issued Photo Identification (Passport) of each Subscriber, Director, and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (RMI is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; documents must be notarized and authenticated in the origin country, then legalized by an RMI Embassy, Consulate, or the RMI Government Liaison Office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Proof of Residential or Business Address (utility invoice or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed financial institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the RMI consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Professional AML Reference, including Source of Funds Declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or regulated professional intermediary (lawyer or accountant) of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the RMI consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or Certificate of Good Standing of any corporate subscriber or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the corporate subscriber's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization, or Hague Apostille if the origin country is an Apostille Contracting Party, followed by certification by the licensed RMI Registered Agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Signature Pages of the Articles of Incorporation and By-Laws, together with the UBO Declaration Form under the Financial Integrity Law
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator or initial directors before a notary public in the place of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the RMI consular authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to Act as Registered Agent and Registered Office (Form Registered Agent-1)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed RMI Registered Agent (Majuro, Marshall Islands)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed domestically in the RMI; notarization accepted in-country, no apostille or consular legalization required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the RMI Financial Integrity Law: the licensed Registered Agent must screen every shareholder, director, and UBO against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the RMI FIU domestic watchlist prior to incorporation. Political Exposed Persons, including senior PEPs, their family members, and close associates as defined by FATF Recommendation 12, trigger enhanced due diligence with senior management approval, source-of-funds verification, and adverse-media screening. Ongoing transaction monitoring, risk re-assessment, and a minimum five-year record retention period apply for the life of the corporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Office of the Registrar of Corporations (RMI Corporate Registry, Majuro; name availability search and clearance processed through licensed RMI Registered Agents using the Registrar's corporate registry system)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English (Latin alphabet) characters, being a combination of words, letters, or numbers, or both letters and numbers (Business Corporations Act Section 10); Roman numerals are permitted; no Marshallese translation or transliteration is statutorily required; the name must end with a corporate identifier such as 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Company', 'Limited', or an approved abbreviation thereof.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed corporate name, the Registered Agent must file a written administrative reconsideration request with the Office of the Registrar of Corporations within 30 days of the rejection, attaching evidence of prior use, trademark ownership, or an alternative revised name. If administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review before the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands under the Business Corporations Act, or alternatively reserve a modified name for a fresh 30-day reservation window. Name reservations may be renewed by written application submitted before the expiry of the current reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for operational purposes. The ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS company may conduct business on a fully virtual, cloud-based model with no physical operational premises. However, the company must maintain a statutory registered office in the Marshall Islands at the physical office address of a licensed Registered Agent in Majuro, which serves as the registered office and service-of-process address. A virtual office arrangement cannot replace the physical registered agent office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: less than 5% annual probability for a tax-exempt Non-Resident Business Corporation with a low-risk AML/CFT profile. Physical on-site inspections are event-driven and occur only upon reasonable suspicion reported to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit or the Registrar of Corporations, not as routine administrative practice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act 1990, Title 51, Marshall Islands Revised Code (ss. 51-101 to 51-187; Articles of Incorporation under s. 51-107; registered office and agent under s. 51-112)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow or capital deposit requirement applies to a non-resident business corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, THAT the Corporation accept the subscription of its Sole Incorporator for 1,000 authorized shares of common stock, par value USD 1.00 per share, and issue such shares as fully paid and non-assessable; FURTHER RESOLVED, THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address of the registered agent in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and that such agent be appointed to accept service of process; FURTHER RESOLVED, THAT the following officers be appointed: President, Treasurer, and Secretary; FURTHER RESOLVED, THAT the President and Treasurer be authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and make all filings required to maintain the Corporation's good standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a written name reservation request for the proposed corporate name and one alternate name. The Registrar searches the corporate registry for conflicting names and, if clear, issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and alternate name
Identification particulars of the proposed incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity, submit a revised name or file the written consent of the prior registrant authorizing use of the conflicting name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RMI-recognized notary public or consular officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator executes the Articles of Incorporation, stating the corporate name, authorized share structure, registered agent name and Majuro address, and initial directors. The signature must be notarized or certified by an authorized consular official before lodgement.
required_dossiers: Notarization or consular certification of signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the executed document contains a defect, the incorporator re-executes a corrected copy with the original signature date; no penalty is imposed if correction precedes lodgement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement with Registrar and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General (filed via licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The licensed registered agent lodges the Articles of Incorporation, Name Reservation Certificate, and consent of registered agent with the Registrar, together with the prescribed USD 200 filing fee. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which constitutes conclusive evidence of corporate existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of correction, the filer has 30 days to cure the deficiency and re-submit without additional registration penalty; failure to cure within the period requires a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Governance Instruments and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors acting by unanimous written consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporator or initial directors adopt the Bylaws and approve the First Board Resolution accepting the share subscription, fixing the registered office and agent, and appointing the President, Treasurer, and Secretary. The executed written consent and share ledger are placed in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Unanimous Written Consent of the Board of Directors
Share certificate ledger and subscription agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a directorship vacancy exists at formation, the incorporator appoints an additional director by written instrument prior to any board action, and the consent is re-executed accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Compliance and Economic Substance Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations and RMI Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the corporation for the annual franchise tax, file the economic substance notification required under RMI economic substance regulations, and confirm non-resident status with no RMI-source revenue. The annual statement and franchise tax payment are due in the month of the anniversary of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Annual corporate statement confirming registered agent continuation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings attract a monetary penalty; file a statement of correction together with the late fee within 30 days of the due date to restore good standing and avoid administrative dissolution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Division of Commerce and Industries, Ministry of Resources and Development, RMI (not engaged; entity conducts remote digital services only)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License under the Business License Act 1990 (inapplicable; non-resident SaaS platform holds no physical operations and derives no RMI gross revenue)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority, Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical installation; EIA registration is not required for pure cloud software and property-management data services under the Environmental Protection Act 1984
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no wastewater, VOC, or solid-waste discharge; service delivery is data-only via third-party cloud infrastructure with no on-island emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required in RMI - no physical premises, employees, or place of business located in the jurisdiction; if a host-country sales office is later opened, the applicable fire safety certification, structural load inspection, and workplace clearance of the host jurisdiction will govern.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Taxation Office (RTO), Ministry of Finance, Majuro, in coordination with the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Commerce and Investment; customs administered by the Marshall Islands Customs Service via the ASYCUDA World electronic clearance platform; no dedicated national e-filing tax portal exists for non-resident entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign parent forms a Marshall Islands Business Corporation (MH_BC) by filing Articles of Incorporation through a licensed Registered Agent and obtaining a Certificate of Incorporation with a registered file number. Because the entity is classified as a Non-Resident Tax-Exempt corporation deriving no Marshall Islands-source revenue, no TIN, VAT ID, or GRT registration is required. Only if the entity commences carrying on business within the Marshall Islands and earns RMI-source gross revenue above the de minimis threshold must it register with the RTO for Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) and file quarterly returns; if it moves physical goods, an Importer/Exporter Number is separately obtained from the Marshall Islands Customs Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: Non-Resident Business Corporation exempt from RMI income tax; the Marshall Islands imposes no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no withholding tax. The only in-rem tax exposure is the Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) at 3% on gross revenue derived from RMI sources only; offshore SaaS subscription revenue is outside the tax base entirely.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Marshall Islands has no check-the-box, entity-classification election, or hybrid-mismatch election. Tax classification is fixed by statute: a Non-Resident Business Corporation with no RMI-source gross revenue has no registration or filing obligation; RMI-source gross revenue is taxed at entity level under the Gross Revenue Tax Act 1986 at 3%.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT, GST, or Sales-and-Use tax exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The direct analog is the Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) at 3% headline on RMI-source gross revenue, administered alongside customs import duties under the Customs Tariff Ordinance; exports and offshore service revenue are excluded from the GRT base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: USD 10,000 of annual gross revenue — de minimis threshold above which a business carrying on business in the Marshall Islands must register for GRT and file quarterly returns. A Non-Resident PropTech SaaS entity with no physical RMI nexus and no RMI-source subscription revenue falls below the registration nexus and is not registrable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. The RMI imposes no mandatory e-invoicing, no real-time fiscal clearance, no digital fiscal stamping, and no tax-API integration. The only electronic clearance mandate is customs-related: import/export declarations must be processed through the ASYCUDA World UNCTAD customs platform, accompanied by standard commercial invoices and packing lists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable as a VAT zero-rating concept because no VAT exists. Under the Gross Revenue Tax Act 1986, 'gross revenue' is statutorily limited to revenue from business transacted within the Marshall Islands; revenue from bona fide export sales and from services supplied to and received by non-residents outside the RMI (including offshore PropTech cloud subscriptions and rental-screening SaaS fees) is excluded from the GRT base and is thus economically zero-rated. Eligibility is established by showing a non-resident customer, foreign payment rails (e.g., Stripe Billing, ACH Direct), no RMI physical performance, no RMI permanent establishment, and no RMI-source counterparty.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: RMI Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World electronic declaration / Form Cus-Exp)
Original Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export from an RMI port
Commercial Invoice stating true export value and non-resident buyer
Marshall Islands Customs Exporter License or Certificate of Incorporation of the Business Corporation
Offshore SaaS subscription contract or platform payment statement evidencing the non-resident service recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The RTO may audit taxpayers and reassess within a six-year retrospective window. Any claim of offshore/export exclusion later found to cover RMI-source revenue triggers reassessment at the 3% GRT rate, an automatic late-payment penalty of 10% of the tax due, and statutory interest. Fraudulent mischaracterization, sham offshore documentation, or falsified export declarations constitute criminal tax evasion under the Gross Revenue Tax Act 1986 and the RMI Penal Code, carrying fines up to USD 5,000, imprisonment up to three years, and revocation of the Certificate of Good Standing. The US-dollar legal-tender regime imposes no foreign-exchange controls; therefore the 180-day benchmark is a substantiation best practice rather than a statutory repatriation deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands does not maintain a central bank. Monetary authority functions are effectively delegated to the United States Federal Reserve System because the US dollar is the sole legal tender. Banking and corporate-house AML/CFT supervision is performed by the Marshall Islands Banking Commissioner and the Financial Intelligence and Investigation Unit (FIIU) within the Ministry of Finance, while currency issuance is not an RMI function.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands adopts full dollarization and applies no exchange-control restrictions. Both current-account transactions (subscription fees, license revenue, SaaS cloud rentals, development fees, vendor payments, and royalties) and capital-account flows (share capital injections, intercompany loans, loan redemptions, dividends, and ownership transfers) are freely convertible and remittable in US dollars. There is no separate domestic currency, no central bank approval, no repatriation permit, and no surrender requirement. Practical hurdles are limited to correspondent-bank due-diligence requests, OFAC screening, and the need to substantiate beneficial ownership and source of funds for ACH/SWIFT transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline exists for any export receipts, including SaaS subscription proceeds, property-management cloud fees, rental-screening data licensing revenue, or intercompany service fees. Export proceeds may remain in foreign bank accounts indefinitely, may be designated solely in USD, and are not subject to mandatory conversion, holding-period minimums, or central bank approval.

Bank of Marshall Islands – Retail/USD Settlement Account
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for USD ACH and Wire Receipts
Operational Account / International USD Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Marshall Islands Development Bank (RMI Development Bank), Domestic Banking Window
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Escrow / Statutory-Fund Account Only (not recommended for SaaS treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium with substantial US-bank dependence. RMI does not license offshore electronic-money institutions, and no standalone EMI/PSP charter exists. A PropTech SaaS treasury can validly use a foreign fintech EMI (e.g., a UK FCA-authorized EMI, EU/EEA EMI, or US money-transmitter-backed BaaS platform) only where the EMI opens a segregated USD omnibus account at a US or correspondent bank and the RMI BC maintains a sub-account or virtual IBAN. The legal constraint is that an EMI is not a licensed Marshall Islands bank and cannot hold RMI client deposits, nor can it provide local settlement services that would otherwise trigger the Banking Act. To remain compliant, the client-facing payment rails must be structured as agent/merchant-of-record arrangements, and all customer funds must be treated as corporate operating cash not as deposit-taking. The EMI must be integrated with Stripe Billing and ACH Direct through a US partner bank; otherwise the RMI entity will face account restriction due to insufficient US nexus.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: RMI statutory practice does not universally require physical presence for corporate account opening; however, most banks and their US correspondent partners require either (a) in-person director identification before a bank officer at Majuro, (b) remote video KYC with notarized certified passport copies, or (c) acceptable legal-person identification through a qualified introducer. The prudential rule is that at least one authorized signatory or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must be available for a remote live interview, and the bank retains discretion to require a physical visit for high-risk jurisdictions or complex corporate ownership structures. For an ISIC 6201 PropTech SaaS entity with a standard Low_Risk_Standard AML tier, remote onboarding is generally feasible when supported by apostilled corporate documents, a certificate of incumbency, bank reference letters, and OFAC-clean passport scans.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO and ownership complexity / offshore holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full ownership chain from UBOs through the Marshalls Business Corporation, certified copies of passports, evidence of the UBO's residential address, a capital-structure diagram, and a legal opinion from RMI counsel confirming no bearer shares or nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SaaS revenue timing mismatch and expected future deposit volume inconsistency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply audited pro-forma ARR reports, PropTech platform subscription contracts, a merchant-of-record agreement with Stripe Billing, portfolio rental-screening transaction logs, and explanation of ACH Direct as the primary debit rail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low physical substance in jurisdiction / non-resident shell indication
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare substance file with executed service agreements, cloud hosting and data sub-processing agreements, minutes of board meetings, an RMI registered-agent certificate, and documented issuable-share ledger showing real economic ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound capital injection from related/founder entities
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce audited source-of-wealth statements, bank statements from the sending institution, executed shareholder loan or subscription agreements, wire-transfer purpose codes, and a clear treasury flow chart to satisfy FIIU beneficial-ownership checks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to international vendors and contractors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide vendor due-diligence file, invoice matching proof, cloud-infrastructure procurement records, SWIFT/MT103 historical examples, and a documented TMS policy showing that all outbound payments are trade-related or operating costs.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed as plain USD wire transfers through a US correspondent bank or via Fedwire/SWIFT MT103, with purpose-code conventions appropriate to a foreign direct investment in a non-resident business corporation. Recommended wire descriptor: 'Capital subscription and paid-in surplus for issuance of common shares – Marshall Islands BC, invoice/reference [BC registration no.]'. When sending through an intermediary, use the RMI bank's correspondent ABA routing number with the explicit account name of the BC. For ACH Direct in the PropTech context, the same receiving account can also accept SaaS working-capital payments from property managers; but any inbound capital injection greater than $50,000 should be transmitted by wire, not ACH, and must be accompanied by a board resolution, share-issuance ledger, and OFAC-compliant source-of-funds evidence. All funds should be credited as 'operating treasury' unless designated for a statutory escrow, in which case the Capital Escrow Account should be used.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements from the RMI BC will occur via three preferred clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for international vendor settlements, subscription-technology licensing, and intercompany treasury sweeps above $50,000; (2) USD correspondent wire through Fedwire for US vendors and strategic service providers; and (3) ACH Direct (ACH debit/credit via a US partner bank or EMI) for high-frequency, low-value customer refunds, rental-screening data access payments, and operational disbursements. Commercial letters of credit (LCs) are not standard for PropTech SaaS operating payments but are permissible if a property-technology enterprise procures heavy hardware or IT equipment from overseas; any such LC must be issued by a US or foreign bank and advised through the RMI commercial bank, with the BC as applicant. Trade settlements must reference the commercial contract and invoice, and banking documentation must always identify the ultimate beneficiary to avoid return-credit suspensions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-only operating treasury negates domestic FX hedging; no permitted RMI-market instruments exist because the US dollar is legal tender.

Cross-currency forward contracts (vanilla FX forwards) on a deliverable basis between USD and EUR/GBP/AUD/CAD can be executed by the offshore treasury function with an OECD-licensed counterparty, provided the RMI BC has genuine transactional FX exposure from SaaS revenues billed in non-USD currencies.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible for emerging-market currencies (e.g., INR, IDR, PHP, KRW) where property-technology clients pay in local currency and the NDF is cash-settled in USD; such instruments must be booked outside the regulated RMI banking book.

Cross-currency swaps (USD vs EUR/GBP) are permissible on an unsecured OTC basis with standard ISDA documentation for long-dated treasury exposures, but only if the swap serves hedge accounting under the financial reporting framework and no speculative leverage is introduced.

Plain-vanilla currency options and barrier options are legally permissible for hedging SAP/HCM SaaS multi-currency revenue streams, but must be authorized by the RMI BC's Treasury Policy and entered into with a top-tier US/EU bank by a delegated officer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of the Business Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands (Office of the Attorney General)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation (filing window opens 30 days prior; must be filed by the last day of the anniversary month)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late penalty for each month or part thereof overdue; continued delinquency beyond 12 months may lead to administrative dissolution by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a non-resident Business Corporation unless the company is listed on a securities exchange or a special resolution of shareholders mandates an audit; otherwise optional.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or US Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (US GAAP) permitted; IFRS is default for cross-border reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Marshall Islands does not maintain a public UBO register; the Registered Agent is required to hold current beneficial ownership details, and the Annual Report must confirm directors, officers, and registered agent. Any share transfer resulting in UBO change must be notified to the Registered Agent for internal record updating, but no separate public UBO filing exists.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 800 - 1,500 USD (typical annual range for Marshall Islands registered agent and registered office services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable by law; voluntary certified audit would cost 3,500 - 8,000 USD depending on volume of transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% on non-resident domestic Business Corporations (BCCA Section 154); the Marshall Islands levies no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no branch-profits tax, and no franchise or net-worth tax on a Non-Resident BC deriving no income from sources within the Republic.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Effective rate is 0%. Non-resident domestic corporations organized under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCCA) are exempt from all taxes of the Republic, including income tax and withholding tax, subject only to the annual corporate report franchise fee graduated by authorized share capital. There is no statutory tax holiday or R&D deduction regime because no tax base exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: BCCA Section 104 Annual Corporate Report (Form AR) filed with the RMI Registrar of Corporations; e-filing is handled through the licensed registered agent portal aligned to the RMI Registrar online system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within the calendar month containing the anniversary date of incorporation; the report must be received by the Registrar before the last day of that month. A late fee is assessed for each month or part of a month of delay.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the corporation, any former names, and the RMI Registry number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as stated in the Articles of Incorporation; no trade names may be substituted on the registry record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address within the Republic and the name and address of the resident Registered Agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Non-Resident BC must maintain a registered office and licensed resident agent in the Marshall Islands; the agent's consent must be current.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital: classes, par value, number of shares issued and outstanding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report exactly the authorized capital schedule; the annual franchise fee is calculated from the authorized share blocks, not from paid-in capital.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and officers: full names, commercial addresses, and positions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No RMI residency is required for directors or officers; use the directors' business addresses, not P.O. boxes; beneficial-ownership data is separately maintained under the RMI AML framework.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business address and global headquarters location.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The principal SaaS operations address may be outside the RMI; an address in the United States is acceptable and creates no RMI income tax nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRS and FATCA self-certification status and any RMI tax-residence declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Non-Resident BC must not declare tax residence in the Republic; beneficiaries must complete the corresponding Form W-8BEN-E and CRS self-certifications.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late fee is imposed under the Registrar's published fee schedule for each overdue month; a second consecutive year of non-filing triggers administrative dissolution under BCCA Section 111; reinstatement requires payment of all arrears, the reinstatement fee, and a petition to the Registrar. Directors of a dissolved corporation are jointly and severally liable for obligations incurred after dissolution under BCCA Section 112.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: RMI Corporate Income Tax Return (RMI Income Tax Act): non-filing status for a Non-Resident BC with no Marshall Islands source income; no RMI Revenue Division form is expected to be submitted. If any Republic-source income is later derived, the return would be filed with the RMI Revenue Division together with the related withholding certificate schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (on a fiscal-year basis identical to the federal taxable year used by the platform group).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: If a filing obligation were triggered, the return is due on the statutory date under the RMI Income Tax Act following the close of the taxable year. For the standard Non-Resident BC profile there is no due date because no taxable income exists within the Republic; a nil return is not required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from sources within the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0. All Stripe Billing and ACH Direct gross receipts relate to foreign customers; SaaS subscription revenue earned through the group's foreign servers and contracts is not sourced to the Republic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions and cost allocations attributable to Marshall Islands source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable; leave zero because no gross income is reportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before statutory exemption.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 and reference BCCA Section 154 exemption; no credit for other foreign taxes is needed because no RMI income tax is imposed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Not applicable in the ordinary Non-Resident BC scenario. If RMI source income is subsequently discovered and the return was willfully omitted, the Income Tax Act penalty regime applies (late filing penalties, interest, and criminal fines for willful evasion); responsible officers face prosecution and restitution orders.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0%. The Republic does not impose dividend withholding tax or any distribution tax on amounts paid by a Non-Resident domestic Business Corporation to its shareholders; dividends may be repatriated in USD without RMI withholding formalities.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The RMI has no comprehensive income tax treaty with the United States or with major EU markets, so no RMI-side DTA relief is available or needed. Where a shareholder resident in a third State seeks source-country treaty benefits for a dividend paid by the RMI BC, the protocol is: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the shareholder's foreign revenue authority (U.S. shareholders use IRS Form 6166); (ii) obtain from the RMI registered agent a Certificate of Good Standing and a certified board resolution declaring the dividend; (iii) deliver a Form W-8BEN-E to the U.S. withholding agent or the foreign payer identifying the RMI BC as flow-through recipient where applicable; (iv) verify Limitation-on-Benefits clauses (active business or ownership and base-erosion tests); and (v) retain the distribution ledger and dividend resolution for not less than seven years. Because the RMI withholding rate is already 0%, the protocol is exclusively an inbound-defense procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% RMI statutory withholding on royalties (software licenses, PropTech platform subscriptions, trademarks) and 0% statutory withholding on interest paid to non-residents. Under the inbound customers' jurisdictions, U.S. source rules apply: copyrighted-software royalties for an enterprise license may be classified as business profits (0%) or as royalties (up to 30% default, potentially reduced to 0-10% by treaty), and U.S. portfolio interest may be exempt while related-party interest under a treaty is generally limited to 0% if the recipient is the beneficial owner, otherwise 30% default. Relevant treaty rates for the group's typical OECD shareholders are: royalties 0-10%, interest 0-15%, subject to beneficial ownership and Limitation-on-Benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No RMI statutory TP documentation threshold exists: the RMI Income Tax Act does not contain transfer pricing rules and the Non-Resident BC has no taxable base. For defense against foreign tax authorities (U.S. IRS Section 482/GILTI, OECD BEPS Actions 8-10, and EU ATAD), the group should voluntarily maintain a Master File and Local File when group intercompany revenue exceeds USD 1,000,000 per annum, and a Country-by-Country Report only when consolidated group revenue exceeds USD 850,000,000 (OECD threshold). A de-minimis threshold of USD 500,000 per intercompany transaction counterparty is recommended for documentation triggers.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The RMI has not enacted Economic Substance Regulations comparable to the BVI or Cayman codes, and the jurisdiction is not placed on the current EU blacklist of non-cooperative jurisdictions. Substance obligations nevertheless arise from: (i) the BCCA requirement to maintain a registered office and licensed resident agent in the Republic (BCCA Section 52); (ii) OECD Global Forum exchange-of-information commitments requiring beneficial ownership records and CRS/FATCA cooperation; and (iii) foreign substance-over-form doctrines under which the U.S. check-the-box rules (Treas. Reg. Sections 301.7701-2 and -3) can recharacterize a thinly capitalized RMI BC, and foreign CFC/GILTI rules (IRC Section 951A) may impose current inclusion on U.S. shareholders regardless of RMI exemption. Board minutes should evidence real decision-making on the Stripe Billing pricing schedule, ACH settlement treasury policies, and vendor contracts to sustain commercial substance if challenged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Tax Evasion / Abuse of the RMI Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the PropTech platform exclusively from the United States while claiming blanket tax immunity on the strength of the RMI Non-Resident BC exemption; treating all Stripe and ACH revenue as non-U.S.-source income without a permanent-establishment analysis; backdating RMI board resolutions or manufacturing offshore minutes to misrepresent management and control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under RMI law, willful false reporting triggers Income Tax Act penalties, criminal fines, and forfeiture; under IRC Section 7201, willful tax evasion is a felony punishable by a fine of up to USD 100,000 (individual) or USD 500,000 (corporation) and imprisonment up to five years; the civil fraud penalty under IRC Section 6663 adds 75% of the underpayment; late-payment interest accrues under IRC Section 6621; State nexus assessments may expose the group to corporate franchise and sales tax liabilities in multiple U.S. states.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with U.S. nexus are exposed under IRC Section 6672 to the 100% trust-fund recovery penalty for withheld taxes; criminal restitution orders and forfeiture of platform assets may be entered; RMI courts will enforce foreign revenue forfeiture claims premised on money laundering predicates; senior officers face travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition requests on tax-fraud warrants.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abusive Substance-Over-Form and U.S. Check-the-Box Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI BC as a paper vehicle with no board activity, no personnel, no contracts in the Republic, and no commercial rationale; failing to file Form 5471 (information return of U.S. persons with respect to foreign corporations) or Form 8858 (disregarded entity) while U.S. owners derive SaaS revenue through the RMI entity; claiming exemption from Federal income tax while exercising full managerial control from the United States.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification as a U.S. domestic corporation under IRC Section 7701(a)(3); retroactive U.S. corporate tax at 21% plus branch-profits tax exposure under IRC Section 884 at 30% on deemed distributions; Form 5471 penalties of USD 10,000 per failure, increased to USD 50,000 after 90-day notice; failure to file Form 8858 carries a USD 10,000 penalty and loss of protective check-the-box elections; GILTI inclusion under IRC Section 951A applies at a 10.5% effective minimum rate plus Subpart F inclusions at 21%, all with compounding interest and precision penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil when the RMI entity is proven to be a mere instrumentality, holding shareholders and directors personally liable for the unpaid corporate tax; responsible officers face the Section 6672 100% penalty; director-level FBAR penalties of up to 50% of undisclosed accounts apply where RMI bank, payment, or treasury accounts are unreported; tax-engaged professionals face injunction and Circular 230 discipline where they have relied on a sham shell structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Sanctions and Beneficial-Ownership Compliance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting subscription and rental-screening payments through Stripe Billing and ACH Direct without performing an AML risk assessment on the landlord client base, screening against OFAC/UN/EU sanctions lists, or maintaining beneficial-ownership records for corporate landlords that own the underlying real estate; failure to submit the required RMI beneficial-ownership information for the Non-Resident BC; processing payments for sanctions-designated persons.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The RMI Money Laundering (Prevention and Control) Act 2003 imposes penalties up to USD 1,000,000 per contravention, plus confiscation and criminal forfeiture and a possible 14-year term of imprisonment; U.S. Bank Secrecy Act penalties reach USD 32,907 per non-willful violation and up to USD 164,508 or 50% of the transaction per willful violation; OFAC penalties reach USD 295,141 per sanctions transaction (or USD 1,177,964 for aggravated cases) plus imprisonment up to 30 years; Stripe and ACH processors will terminate merchant accounts upon any BSA/OFAC event, leaving refund liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal money-laundering prosecution in the RMI (up to 14 years' imprisonment) and extradition risk from allied jurisdictions; OFAC designation leads to asset freezes and travel restrictions; directors who funnel rental-screening fees for sanctioned landlords may be debarred from professional services and from owning or servicing U.S. payment accounts; mandatory disqualification of directors following AML enforcement actions in foreign jurisdictions collaterally invalidates appointments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Registry Non-Compliance and Administrative Dissolution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the BCCA Section 104 annual report within the anniversary month; failure to remit the graduated franchise fee; continuing to bill PropTech subscription fees through Stripe and ACH after administrative dissolution of the RMI entity; using the bank account of a dissolved BC as a settlement pass-through while failing to reinstate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution under BCCA Section 111 after continued default; late fee applicable monthly under the Registrar's fee schedule; reinstatement only upon payment of all arrears, reinstatement fees, and the issuance of a restoration certificate; obligations entered into after dissolution are voidable; RMI financial institutions freeze a settled account upon registry notice of dissolution; the U.S. IRS may retroactively treat the dissolved entity as a partnership or disregarded entity producing a taxable deemed liquidation event.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for all obligations incurred after the dissolution date under BCCA Section 112; continuing to dividend or clear ACH settlements after dissolution constitutes fraudulent misrepresentation exposing directors to civil restitution; the RMI High Court may issue travel bans in registry-fraud or money-laundering investigations; directors are personally responsible for reinstatement costs and for refunds to customers on voidable platform contracts.
